renders._yaml:
- component: figure
  title: Variant distributions per caller
  description: |-
    Each panel is one bcftools distribution (indel length, substitution, read depth, allele frequency, singletons), and each bar the number of variant records in one of its bins, grouped by caller. It answers how the call sets of different callers are distributed.
    How to read: every panel has its own axes, because the sections count different kinds of records on different scales; compare callers within a panel. Callers that peak in the same bins agree, and a caller with an extra mode, for instance very low allele frequencies, adds calls the others do not make.
    Lines and annotations: no reference line is drawn, because a median of bin counts says nothing about a distribution.
    Source: https://samtools.github.io/bcftools/bcftools.html
  code: |-
    # the x value of a section: its label when it has one (categorical sections and
    # the open-ended depth bucket), else its numeric bin
    d = df.with_columns(
        pl.coalesce([pl.col("label"), pl.col("bin").map_elements(lambda v: f"{v:g}", return_dtype=pl.Utf8)]).alias("key")
    ).drop_nulls(["key", "count"]).sort(["section", "bin", "label"], nulls_last=True)
    fig = px.bar(
        d.to_pandas(),
        x="key",
        y="count",
        color="caller",
        barmode="group",
        facet_col="section",
        facet_col_wrap=2,
        facet_row_spacing=0.14,
        facet_col_spacing=0.08,
        labels={"key": "Bin", "count": "Variant records", "caller": "Caller", "section": "Section"},
    )
    fig.for_each_annotation(lambda a: a.update(text=a.text.split("=", 1)[-1].replace("_", " ")))
    fig.update_xaxes(matches=None, showticklabels=True, title_text="", type="category")
    fig.update_yaxes(matches=None, showticklabels=True, title_text="")
    fig.update_layout(margin={"t": 32, "l": 48, "r": 16, "b": 32})

- component: card
  title: Records in the distributions
  description: |-
    The hero number is the variant records counted in the distributions in view, and the bars rank the sections by the records they hold, with the median and maximum bin beside it. It answers how large the selected distributions are.
    How to read: each section counts a different kind of record, such as sites, SNPs or substitutions, so a sum across sections is not a variant count. Filter to one section for a figure that means something.
  column: count
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: section
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: sections with the most records

- component: table
  title: Distribution bins
  description: |-
    Each row is a bin of one distribution for one sample and caller, with its section, its numeric or categorical label and the records it holds. It answers the exact value behind the bar chart.
    How to read: filter by section, then sort by count to find the most populated bins.

- component: figure
  title: SNPs per caller
  description: |-
    Each bar is the number of SNP records one caller reports for one sample, coloured by sample. It answers how productive each caller is and whether the ranking holds across samples.
    How to read: callers on the same sample should land in the same order of magnitude. A caller far above the others may be calling noise, and one far below may be missing variants, so confirm with the Ts/Tv tile.
    Source: https://samtools.github.io/bcftools/bcftools.html
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: caller
    y: n_snps
    color: sample
    barmode: group
    labels:
      caller: Caller
      n_snps: SNP records
      sample: Sample

- component: card
  title: SNP records
  description: |-
    The hero number is the SNP records over every caller and sample, and the bars rank the callers by the SNPs they report. It answers which caller finds the most SNPs.
    How to read: more calls is not better calls. Compare with the Ts/Tv tile and with the indel count before preferring a caller.
  column: n_snps
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: caller
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: callers with the most SNPs

- component: card
  title: Indel records
  description: |-
    The hero number is the indel records over every caller and sample, and the bars rank the callers by the indels they report. It answers which caller finds the most indels.
    How to read: callers differ more on indels than on SNPs, so a large spread here is common. Check the indel length distribution before trusting the largest count.
  column: n_indels
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: caller
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: callers with the most indels

- component: card
  title: Multiallelic sites
  description: |-
    The hero number is the sites carrying more than one alternate allele, and the ring splits them by caller. It answers which callers report multiallelic sites.
    How to read: a caller with a large share splits sites into several alleles where others do not. A caller with none may not support multiallelic calls.
  column: n_multiallelic_sites
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: caller
  caption: multiallelic sites, by caller

- component: advanced_viz
  id: caller_yield_dotplot
  title: Variant yield per caller and sample
  description: |-
    Each dot is one caller on one sample, sized by the share of its records that are SNPs and coloured by the log10 of its record count. It answers how much a caller finds and how its calls split between SNPs and other variants.
    How to read: a big dot is a SNP dominated call set and a small one holds many indels or other records. A pale or dark dot shows a caller that finds fewer or more records than its peers on the same sample.
  kind: dot_plot
  roles:
    cluster: sample
    gene: caller
    mean_expression: log10_n_records
    frac_expressing: snp_fraction

- component: table
  title: Variant counts per caller
  description: |-
    Each row is one caller on one sample, with its record, SNP, MNP, indel, multiallelic and other counts, the SNP fraction and the log10 of the records. It answers the exact numbers behind every other tile.
    How to read: sort by records to compare callers within a sample.

- component: figure
  title: Ts/Tv ratio per caller
  description: |-
    Each bar is the ratio of transitions to transversions among the SNPs of one caller on one sample, coloured by sample. It answers whether callers agree on the substitution balance of the SNPs they report.
    How to read: the cited study uses the ratio as a quality indicator for SNP calls, so callers run on the same sample are expected to land close together. A caller far from its peers is adding or losing SNPs of one kind, a sign of noise or bias. A bar of 0 is a caller with too few SNPs to score.
    Note: the ratio varies with genome region, gene function and GC content, so no single cut-off applies and no reference line is drawn.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25297068/
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: caller
    y: ts_tv
    color: sample
    barmode: group
    labels:
      caller: Caller
      ts_tv: Transition/transversion ratio
      sample: Sample

- component: card
  title: Typical Ts/Tv ratio
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median transition/transversion ratio over the callers and samples that have a ratio, and the box shows the spread. It answers how the SNP call sets balance transitions and transversions.
    How to read: a wide box means callers disagree. Callers scored 0 for lack of SNPs are left out so they do not pull the median down.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25297068/
  column: ts_tv
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  filter_expr: col('ts_tv') > 0
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: table
  title: Ts/Tv per caller
  description: |-
    Each row is one caller on one sample, with its transition and transversion counts and the ratio, over all alternates and over the first alternate only. It answers the exact numbers behind the other tiles.
    How to read: sort by ratio to find the callers that depart from the others.
